clean_story:
Flying rivers. Sky waterfalls.

The name atmospheric river comes from their shape—long, narrow bands of moisture in the sky, like a river flowing above land. They carry water vapor from the tropics to higher latitudes, dumping rain or snow when they hit mountains or cold air. A single one can transport 15 times the water of the Mississippi River. In 2023, California’s relentless storms were fueled by a series of these, dropping 30 inches of rain in some areas. Satellites track them by measuring water vapor, watching as they stretch thousands of miles, invisible until they unleash floods or refill reservoirs. Their width is often just 250 miles, yet they deliver up to 50 percent of annual precipitation in places like the western United States.

Three related subjects are pineapple express, bomb cyclones and weather satellites.
